chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: Ideas versus personalities
summary: Sauter prefers not to talk like a tabloid.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: When we discussed historical affairs such as we have been, it seems to me that it gets involved with personalities more than ideas, and as far as I'm concerned, most of my life I have not been concerned too much with personalities

I think so too. Why it happens I don't know, but when we go way back, we sort of forget what it felt like to live there, in talking about people. I would prefer to talk about them--oh, I don't know; let's go on.
In maybe a more impersonal fashion, do you mean?
Not necessarily impersonal, but not too much like tabloid newspapers.
We'll t-y to avoid New York Post in an interview.
